desc:
A row of wizards has individual strengths given by strength. The strength of a contiguous group is defined as (the weakest wizard in the group) × (the sum of all strengths in the group).

Return the sum of the strengths of all non-empty contiguous groups, modulo 1,000,000,007.

Example: for [1, 3, 1, 2] the answer is 44. For [5, 4, 6] it is 213.
hints: The number of groups is O(n<sup>2</sup>); for n = 100,000 you need something like O(n). Use the contribution idea: handle all groups at once by the position of their weakest wizard.

For wizard i, let L and R be the boundaries within which it is the minimum (tie-break so each group has one owner). The groups it owns are all [l, r] with L < l ≤ i ≤ r < R. You need the sum of the group sums over this whole family, multiplied by strength[i].

With prefix sums P, a group sum is P[r+1] - P[l]. Summing it over all pairs (l, r) needs sums of consecutive prefix sums, so build prefix sums Q of P. Then the total over the family is (i-L) * (sum of P[i+1..R]) - (R-i) * (sum of P[L+1..i]), each a difference of two Q values.
editorial: Let L be the nearest index on the left with a strictly smaller strength (or -1) and R the nearest index on the right with a smaller-or-equal strength (or n); with this tie-break each group is owned by exactly one wizard. Wizard i owns every group [l, r] with L < l ≤ i and i ≤ r < R, and contributes strength[i] * sum(group sums).

Let P[t] be the sum of the first t strengths, and Q[t] = P[0] + ... + P[t-1]. Then summing over r and l independently gives total group sums (i - L) * (Q[R+1] - Q[i+1]) - (R - i) * (Q[i+1] - Q[L+1]): the first term adds P[r+1] for each of the i - L choices of l, the second subtracts P[l] for each of the R - i choices of r. The boundaries L and R come from monotonic stacks. The whole thing is O(n) time and space. Python integers are unbounded; in fixed-width languages keep all values reduced modulo 109+7 and take care with the subtraction.
solution:
def totalStrength(strength):
    MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
    n = len(strength)
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, x in enumerate(strength):
        P[i + 1] = P[i] + x
    Q = [0] * (n + 2)
    for t in range(n + 1):
        Q[t + 1] = Q[t] + P[t]
    left = [-1] * n    # nearest strictly smaller on the left
    right = [n] * n    # nearest smaller-or-equal on the right
    stack = []
    for i in range(n):
        while stack and strength[stack[-1]] >= strength[i]:
            right[stack.pop()] = i
        left[i] = stack[-1] if stack else -1
        stack.append(i)
    total = 0
    for i in range(n):
        L, R = left[i], right[i]
        sums = (i - L) * (Q[R + 1] - Q[i + 1]) - (R - i) * (Q[i + 1] - Q[L + 1])
        total += strength[i] * sums
    return total % MOD
